concepts.def: A Texas county's economic-development contract under Local Government Code Chapter 381: the county grants tax rebates or other incentives to a developer in exchange for investment and jobs. The Greenport airport campus sits under one signed in 2010.
The US advanced-manufacturing production credit: a per-unit federal tax credit for domestically made battery cells, modules, and components — the incentive pulling battery manufacturing onshore.

The highest transmission voltage in common use in the United States. A 765 kV line carries several times the power of a 345 kV line on one right-of-way with lower losses, which is why it is the backbone choice when a region must move gigawatts across hundreds of miles. AEP built and operates most of the country's existing 765 kV network; Texas chose it in 2025 for the Permian Basin plan.

The next-generation data-center power architecture: distributing 800-volt direct current to the rack instead of low-voltage AC. Higher voltage means lower current and losses, fewer conversion stages, and far less copper for megawatt-class racks.

A refrigerant safety class meaning low toxicity and mild flammability. Most low-GWP replacements fall in it, which brings leak detection, ventilation and charge limits into the machine room and into the building code.

A rectifier built from switching transistors rather than plain diodes, so the equipment behind it can draw a near-sinusoidal current at close to unity power factor instead of pulling in gulps. It is what lets a modern UPS or drive stop being a dirty load on the supply feeding it, at the cost of more silicon and more control software.

Anti-dumping and countervailing duties: US trade remedies against imports priced below fair value or subsidized at home. Even a petition creates pricing risk, because duties can apply retroactively to goods already entered.
Pre-wetting the air entering an air-cooled condenser or dry cooler so it arrives closer to wet-bulb. It buys much of a tower's efficiency on the hottest days while using water only on those days.

A chemical added to a concrete mix to change how it behaves — plasticisers for flow, retarders and accelerators for setting time, air entrainment for freeze resistance. It is how one mix serves many conditions.

A power-generation gas turbine derived from an aircraft engine rather than designed as a heavy industrial frame. Lighter and far quicker to start than a heavy-duty machine, in blocks of roughly tens of megawatts — and because the cores can come from retiring airliners, sourceable outside the heavy-frame factory queue that sets everyone else's delivery date.

Allowance for funds used during construction: the financing cost a utility is allowed to add to the price of a plant while it is being built, so the plant enters rate base at construction cost plus the interest and equity return accrued during the build. It is a non-cash earning until the plant enters service.
aliases: allowance for funds used during construction

concepts.def: Absorbent glass mat: the construction that made lead-acid sealed. The electrolyte is held in a glass-fibre mat between the plates and the oxygen made at one plate recombines at the other instead of escaping, so the cell never needs topping up.
Authority having jurisdiction: whichever local official actually enforces the code on this site. Codes are national, interpretations are local, and it is the interpretation that has to be satisfied.
The North American standard that fixes the conditions a water-cooled chiller is rated at and the weighting used for its part-load number, so that two manufacturers' figures can be compared at all.
A UK government designation for an area given faster planning and priority grid access to attract AI data centers. It changes the permitting and connection timeline, not the price of power.

The US law directing a stepwise phasedown of high-GWP hydrofluorocarbon production and imports, with sector rules restricting what new equipment may be charged with. It sets the calendar the whole HVAC industry is redesigning against.

The continuous layer that stops air leaking through a building envelope. In a building full of dry heat it governs how much outdoor moisture arrives uninvited, and it must be continuous to work at all.
High-voltage switchgear whose live parts are separated by open air, so the clearances — and therefore the land — grow with the voltage. Cheap per bay and expensive per hectare.

The authorization from a state or local air agency that a combustion source needs before it can be built and run, written around what leaves the stack — chiefly nitrogen oxides and particulates — and around how many hours it may run. For an on-site power plant it is usually the longest lead item after the machines themselves, and its terms decide whether the same engine may be used as backup only or as prime power.

The return on equity a commission authorizes a utility to earn on its rate base — typically nine to ten percent in recent US decisions. Because it multiplies every dollar of plant, a tenth of a point moves tens of millions a year on a large utility, which is why the return is the most litigated number in a rate case.

The generating end of a gen-set: the rotating machine that turns the engine's mechanical power into alternating current. It is specified separately from the engine — its winding pitch, insulation class and reactance decide how far voltage dips when a large load lands and how much fault current it can push to trip a breaker.

The current a conductor is allowed to carry continuously without exceeding its insulation's temperature limit. It falls when conductors are bundled, run hot, or run in a hot room — so the same cable is not the same rating everywhere.

The one large customer whose signed commitment lets a developer finance and build a site. Its credit becomes the project's credit — and its departure, or the substitution of a different anchor, changes everything the lenders underwrote.

Grid services beyond plain energy — holding capacity in reserve, correcting frequency second by second — that a system operator buys from fast resources such as batteries. In ERCOT they were most of a battery's income until so many batteries arrived that the prices collapsed.

Protection that stops an on-site generator from continuing to energize a utility line after the utility has disconnected. It exists to protect line workers, and it is why a set that runs in parallel with the grid needs more relaying than one that only ever runs on a dead bus.

Volts times amps, measured in kVA — the total current a supply must carry, whether or not that current does useful work. Real power (kW) is the part that becomes work or heat in the load; the ratio of the two is the power factor. Equipment is sized on apparent power because copper and semiconductors heat on current, but the customer buys real power.

The gap between the temperature a heat exchanger achieves and the theoretical best it could achieve — tower water above wet-bulb, or leaving water above refrigerant temperature. Closing an approach costs surface area and money.

At a heat exchanger, the temperature gap between the two fluids that drives heat across it — at a CDU, how much warmer the coolant leaving for the racks is than the facility water arriving from the plant. A capacity rating is only meaningful at a stated approach, and the rack's inlet limit minus the CDU's approach is the warmest water the plant is allowed to make.

The explosive release of energy when current jumps through the air between conductors — a blast hot enough to be lethal at a panel door. An arc-flash study calculates that energy at every piece of gear so the right protective clothing and breaker settings can be specified, and it has to be redone whenever the electrical system changes.

Switchgear built and type-tested so that an internal arcing fault vents its pressure and hot gas away from anyone standing at the door, usually upward through a plenum or duct. The standard is IEEE C37.20.7, and it grades enclosures by which sides are protected and whether the protection survives with a low-voltage door open. It does not stop the arc — it redirects what the arc produces.
The refrigeration-systems safety standard that governs machine rooms: charge limits, refrigerant detection, ventilation and relief. It is the reason a refrigerant change is a building change.
The North American energy standard that sets the minimum full-load and part-load efficiency a chiller may legally have, by type and size. It is the floor every catalogue is written against.

ASHRAE's classification of the water temperature liquid-cooled IT equipment will accept: since the fifth edition the number is the maximum supply temperature in °C (W17, W27, W32, W40, W45 and W+ above 45 °C), all starting at 2 °C. A rack's class fixes how warm the facility water may be, and so whether the plant needs chillers.

A firm that invests other people's money — pension funds, insurers, sovereign funds — through funds it manages for a fee. Goldman Sachs Asset Management is the arm of the bank that runs such funds; when it 'owns' GridStor, the owners are really the fund's investors.
A DC link joining two AC networks that are not — and need not be — in step with one another. It moves power between them while keeping their disturbances on their own sides.

Automatic transfer switch: the device that senses utility failure, signals the generators to start, and moves the load onto them once generation is stable — then manages the return trip when utility power comes back. It is the conductor of a data center's outage choreography.
Adding new battery capacity to an operating storage plant to offset degradation, keeping the plant at its contracted capacity over its life.

The automatic voltage regulator: the controller that adjusts the alternator's field current to hold output voltage steady as load changes. When a data hall lands in one step, the AVR's speed of response is what decides whether the voltage dip stays inside what the IT load and the UPS will accept.

How long a UPS can carry its rated load from stored energy alone — seconds for a flywheel, minutes for a battery string. It is sized to cover the generator's start with a margin, not to run the hall: a longer autonomy is insurance against the engine failing its first start attempt, and it is bought in battery cabinets and floor space.

A contracted promise about the fraction of hours a plant will be ready to perform, with money attached to missing it. It matters more than an average suggests, because storage and generation revenue concentrate into a small number of extreme-price hours — a site that is available almost all year and unavailable for the wrong afternoon has not lost a proportional share of its income.

What happens when a switch is pushed past its breakdown voltage and conducts anyway, dissipating the energy in the process. Some devices are rated to survive a stated amount of it; exceeding that rating destroys the part.

The capacity-weighted number of years left on a portfolio's contracts. A buyer of a contracted platform is buying those years of fixed cash flow; the shorter the average, the sooner the assets become merchant.

Debt raised above the project, at the developer's holding company, secured on the developer's share of project cash flows rather than on the project itself. It lets an owner borrow again without disturbing the project-level lenders.

Everything at a power project other than the main generating or storage equipment: transformers, switchgear, cabling, foundations, roads, controls. In a battery project the batteries are the equipment and the substation and enclosures are balance of plant.

The entity that keeps generation and load matched second by second inside a defined area of the grid. In an RTO region the RTO is the balancing authority; outside one, a large vertically integrated utility can be its own — it dispatches its own plants, holds its own reserves and has no organized capacity market to buy from.

Whether lenders and investors will finance a project or accept a supplier — a function of certifications, warranties, balance-sheet strength, track record, and policy exposure rather than spec-sheet performance.

A special-purpose vehicle set up to hold one lease, loan or asset so that if it fails, its problems stay inside it and do not reach the parent — and so that the parent's problems do not reach it. Lenders and landlords insist on one so the credit they analyse is the one they get.
The engineering document that fixes a project's architecture, ratings and equipment choices before anything is tendered. Whoever writes it decides what the bidders are allowed to offer.

Studying a group of interconnection requests together rather than one at a time, so the effect of all of them on the same corridor is modelled at once. ERCOT proposed batching large-load requests in 2025 after serial studies could not keep up; the price is that every request in the batch waits for the slowest.

Cells or blocks wired in series to make the voltage a UPS needs. The same current passes through all of them, so the string's runtime is set by its weakest cell — which is the entire reason cell monitoring exists.

Battery backup unit: a small battery shelf inside the rack itself, carrying the servers for seconds rather than minutes — long enough to cover a transfer or ride out a disturbance. It moves the last line of stored energy from the UPS room to the point of use.
How much pressure the ground can carry before it fails or settles unacceptably, in pounds per square foot or kilopascals. It sets whether a structure sits on spread footings, a mat, or piles.

The date by which a project must start physical work (or meet the tax rules' safe harbour) to qualify for a tax credit that is being phased out. The 2025 law set 4 July 2026 for wind and solar credits; a project that misses it loses the credit.

Generation or storage connected on the customer's side of the utility meter, serving the site directly — like on-site power at a data-center campus — versus front-of-the-meter assets selling into the grid.

Battery energy storage system: a grid-connected battery plant — cells packaged into modules and enclosures plus power conversion, thermal management, and controls. Rated in MW (power) and MWh (energy).

A switch that floods its drift region with both kinds of charge carrier to conduct, like an IGBT. The flooding gives a low voltage drop at high current regardless of rating, but the stored charge has to be removed at turn-off, which costs time and energy.

Restarting a dead network with no outside power to draw on: small units boot first to energize controls and fuel systems, then larger machines and load return in stages. Rarely exercised on the grid and definitional for an island or a microgrid, which has nothing else to start from.

The share of a generator's rating that can be applied in a single step without voltage and frequency sagging past what the load tolerates. A set that accepts 100 percent block load can pick up a whole data hall at once; one that cannot must have the load added in stages by the transfer or paralleling controls.
Water deliberately discharged from a cooling tower to stop dissolved solids concentrating without limit. It plus evaporation and drift is where a plant's water consumption goes.

Battery management system: the electronics that watch every cell's voltage, current, and temperature, balance the cells, and disconnect the battery when limits are crossed — the battery's safety and health guardian.

A diode that exists inside every power MOSFET as a by-product of how it is built. It conducts current backwards through the device, which is useful in some circuits and a source of loss in others, because it takes time to stop conducting when the voltage reverses.

Bill of materials — the itemised list of every part in a product with its manufacturer and part number. Who controls it decides who can substitute a part, who sees what each part costs, and how hard it is to move the product to another factory.

Assembling finished units — enclosure, boards, wiring, cooling, labels and packaging — rather than just circuit boards. It is a step up the value chain from board assembly and puts the manufacturer in charge of the product the customer actually ships.

The thermodynamic cycle a gas turbine runs on: compress air, add heat by burning fuel in it, expand the hot gas through a turbine, exhaust what is left. Roughly half the turbine's output is consumed driving its own compressor, and efficiency rises with both the pressure ratio and the temperature the machine can survive at — which is why turbine development is largely a materials problem.
The route length beyond which a DC link's cheaper conductors and lower losses outweigh the cost of its two converter stations. Below it AC wins on cost; above it DC does.

The voltage a switch can hold off before it conducts uncontrollably. Designers never run a device near it: a bus voltage plus its switching overshoot is usually kept below about 80% of the rating, so an 800-volt bus needs a device rated well above 800 volts.

On-site generation installed to carry a campus through the years before its grid connection matures, after which the site converts to grid supply and the same plant becomes its backup. The gear and the permits are typically sized for a run of a few years, so the contract is temporary even when the machines are not.

A site that already carries industrial infrastructure — most valuably an existing grid connection and substation from a retired plant. In a market where interconnection is the long pole, inheriting energized wires can move a project years ahead of an equivalent greenfield, which is why retired coal and industrial sites are being bought for their electrical position rather than their land.

The workhorse step-down switching converter: a switch chops the input on and off thousands to millions of times a second, and an inductor and capacitor smooth the chopped pulses into a lower steady voltage set by the fraction of time the switch is on. Several bucks running out of step with each other — a multiphase buck — share the current and cancel each other's ripple, which is how the regulators beside a processor deliver hundreds of amps.

A model in which the vendor finances, builds, owns and runs the plant and sells the output, rather than selling the plant to a utility. The customer buys electricity and the vendor keeps the technology and the risk.

A procurement structure in which a developer builds a generation or storage project and then transfers ownership to the utility at commercial operation. It gives the utility rate-based ownership without carrying construction risk, and gives the developer a defined exit. The middle option between a purchase agreement, where the utility never owns the asset, and a self-build, where it carries every risk.
How much energy has been extracted from a given mass of fuel before it is discharged, in gigawatt-days per tonne. Higher burnup means fewer refuellings and less spent fuel per unit of electricity.

A DC-DC stage that steps a distribution voltage down by a fixed ratio, like a transformer for direct current, without trying to hold its output constant. Giving up regulation lets it run at its resonant sweet spot with very high efficiency and density; a separate regulator elsewhere in the chain does the holding.

A solid bar of copper or aluminum used instead of cable to carry very large currents over short distances inside equipment, a rack, or a switchboard. It is the same idea as facility busway one scale smaller and inside the machine, and its cross-section is the only thing standing between the current and the heat that current makes.

Prefabricated bus bar running overhead along a row of racks, with tap-off boxes that branch power down to each cabinet. It replaces bundles of individually pulled feeders, so capacity can be added or moved without rewiring — which is why the 800 VDC designs distribute at the row on busway rather than conduit.
How fast a battery charges or discharges relative to its capacity: 1C empties it in one hour, 0.25C in four. Grid storage typically runs at low C-rates — multi-hour durations rather than sprints.

The current an AC cable draws simply to charge its own capacitance, growing with length and voltage. Beyond roughly a hundred kilometres of subsea cable it consumes the whole rating, which is why long submarine links are direct current.

A binding contract to supply a stated amount of compute or power for a stated period at agreed terms — the document a lender will finance against, as opposed to an announcement, an option or a letter of intent.
The fraction of a generator's nameplate that a grid planner is willing to count on at the moment of system peak. Firm plant approaches its nameplate; weather-dependent plant does not.

The energy a plant actually produced over a period divided by what it would have produced running flat out the whole time. A nuclear unit near 90 percent runs almost continuously; a solar farm in the 20s runs only when the sun does; a peaker in single digits runs only on the hardest days.

A market that pays a resource for being available to serve peak demand — a payment for existing, not for energy produced. PJM runs its auction, the Base Residual Auction, three years ahead; the clearing price per megawatt-day is the signal that new data-center load has moved the region from surplus to scarcity, and it flows straight into a regulated utility's bills.

A real timed discharge into a load bank, measured against the rating — the only measurement that proves what a string will actually do. The IEEE stationary-battery practices set the method and the interval, and the industry retires a string at eighty percent of rated capacity.
Selling a finished or late-stage asset to release the equity tied up in it and reinvest in new development. For a developer without a fund behind it, recycling is the main source of growth capital.
A developer that builds only for its parent or one customer rather than for the market. It trades the ability to sell to anyone for a guaranteed buyer and the parent's balance sheet.
Splitting a business so a buyer takes one part and the sellers keep the rest as a separate company. What goes with which side — assets, contracts, people, supply orders — is the whole negotiation.

A California local-government body that buys electricity for its residents while the utility still owns the wires. CCAs sign resource-adequacy and storage contracts of their own, so they are buyers of batteries alongside the utilities.

Certificate of convenience and necessity: Texas's name for the commission order that lets a utility build a specific line or, outside ERCOT, a plant. In ERCOT it is issued for transmission — a wires-only utility's CCN case decides the route and the need for a 345 kV or 765 kV line, never a generator.

Coolant distribution unit: the heat exchanger and pump station that separates the facility's water loop from the clean liquid loop feeding the servers, delivering coolant to the cold plates at the right temperature and pressure. It is the interface that lets one facility cooling spine serve many different rack designs.

Arkansas's certificate of environmental compatibility and public need — the state's version of a CPCN, the commission order a utility must obtain before building a major generating plant or transmission line and putting it in rate base.
aliases: certificate of environmental compatibility and public need

concepts.def: A compressor that raises pressure by flinging refrigerant outward with a high-speed impeller. Very efficient at large capacities and smooth flow, and it has a lower flow limit below which it cannot maintain head.

The California Environmental Quality Act: every discretionary permit in California needs an environmental review — a negative declaration or a full impact report — before it can be issued. It is where a battery project's fire, noise and traffic questions get answered in public.

Minnesota's version of the certificate: the commission's finding that a specific large plant or line is needed, issued in its own docket after the resource plan has set the direction. A combustion turbine or a transmission line in Minnesota needs one before it can be built and recovered.
The document that makes a building legally usable. Everything from a fire pump test to a landscaping condition can hold it up, and no amount of finished construction substitutes for it.
A self-sustaining sequence in which each fission releases neutrons that cause further fissions. A reactor is held at exactly one fission per fission — any more and power rises, any less and it falls.

A clause in a loan or contract that lets the other party renegotiate or walk away if the company's owner changes. Debt priced on one sponsor's name is re-examined when a different sponsor buys the platform.
A formal amendment to the contract's scope, price or schedule. Their number and cause is the honest measure of how complete a design was when construction started.

A Texas county or city agreement to waive most of a new project's property taxes for up to ten years in exchange for the investment and jobs. Counties attach conditions — cooling technology, water use, road repairs — and can claw the taxes back if they are broken.
The temperature of the water a chiller sends out to the coils or the CDUs. Raising it is the single cheapest efficiency lever in a plant, and its ceiling is set by what the load can accept.

The minutes a chilled-water plant needs after a power interruption before it is making cooling again, because compressors cannot be restarted instantly. It is the thermal analogue of the ten-second race on the power side.
The control logic that decides how many machines run and which ones. Getting it wrong is the difference between a plant at design efficiency and one running four machines lightly loaded.

A financing entity that borrows money, buys AI accelerators and leases them to the company that uses them. It keeps the chips off the user's balance sheet; the lenders' risk is what the chips are worth when the lease ends.

Combined heat and power, also called cogeneration: using both the electricity a prime mover generates and the heat it would otherwise vent. Because the heat is free once the fuel is burned, overall fuel utilisation can pass 80 percent — but only if there is a real use for the heat next door, which is what makes siting rather than efficiency the binding question.
The treatment step in which suspended solids are allowed or induced to settle out of water. It is the workhorse ahead of filtration in nearly every water and wastewater train.

Generation that is both low-carbon and available on demand around the clock — nuclear, geothermal, hydro, or a fuel-burning plant with capture. It is what a load with a flat, continuous profile actually needs.

A transfer that closes onto the new source before opening the old one, so the two are briefly in parallel and the load never sees a break. It requires the generator to be synchronized to the utility first, and the utility's permission, because for a fraction of a second the site's engines are feeding the grid.

A delivery method in which the construction manager joins during design as an adviser and then converts into the builder under a price it guarantees. The owner buys preconstruction advice and price certainty from the same firm.

The Texas rule under which a generator and a large customer on the same site settle only the net flow with the grid — generation minus load — subject to regulator review. It decides whether a campus can use its own power before the grid sees it.

The date a project is declared complete, tested and delivering to the grid under its contracts. Debt converts from construction to term, revenue starts, and the developer's delivery promise is either kept or late.

Coefficient of performance: heat moved divided by work put in. A chiller at a COP of 6 moves six units of heat per unit of electricity — it is moving heat, not making it, which is why the number exceeds one.

A customer's demand at the moment the whole system peaks, as opposed to its own highest hour. Transmission and capacity costs are allocated on it, so a flat load such as a data center that draws the same at the system peak as at 3 a.m. is charged a full share — and a load that can back off for the peak hours can shed a large part of its bill.

A liquid-cooled metal block clamped directly onto a processor, carrying heat away in a coolant loop instead of an air stream. Above roughly 100 kW per rack air physically cannot move the heat fast enough, so liquid has to touch the silicon.
Data-center space, power, and cooling leased to tenants who bring their own IT equipment. Colocation providers are the landlords of the AI buildout.

Two heat engines on one fuel: a gas turbine burns the gas, and its hot exhaust then boils water to spin a second, steam turbine. Recovering that otherwise-wasted heat pushes modern plants past 60 percent efficiency — the highest of any gas machine — at the cost of far more equipment and a much longer build than simple cycle.

The one-step US route in which permission to build and permission to operate are granted together, against inspections and tests agreed in advance. It removes the risk of a finished plant that cannot be allowed to run.

The structured testing that proves a finished plant performs as contracted before it is handed over and paid for. For storage it is where capacity and round-trip-efficiency guarantees are measured; for a data center it is where the outage choreography gets rehearsed rather than discovered in production.

Densifying placed soil so it will carry load without settling later, verified in the field against a laboratory maximum. Fill that was not compacted to specification shows up as a cracked slab years afterwards.

A sponsor's promise to lenders that a project will be finished, or that a capped amount will be paid if it is not. It covers the construction period, when there is no rent yet to secure the debt; it is not a guarantee of the debt itself.
A buyer's contractual promise to purchase a stated amount of computing capacity or spend a stated sum over years — the demand-side document that suppliers, landlords and lenders finance against.

The property that any single component can be taken out of service for planned work without dropping the critical load — the defining requirement of Uptime Tier III. It is decided by topology rather than by equipment quality: there must be a second path, and the switch onto it must itself be safe.
The heat exchanger where the compressed refrigerant gives its heat up and turns back into a liquid — to outdoor air in an air-cooled machine, to tower water in a water-cooled one.
Letting condenser water get colder when the weather allows, which lowers the lift and so the compressor work. It is most of why a chiller's part-load efficiency beats its full-load efficiency.

A lender's promise to lend once a list of conditions is met — for the DOE Loan Programs Office, the stage between approval and closing. It can be withdrawn before closing, as Grain Belt Express's USD 4.9 billion guarantee was in July 2025.

Local government's permission to build something a zoning code does not allow by right. For a battery it is usually decided by a county board or city commission after a public hearing, and it is where community opposition can stop a project outright.

The list of things that must be true before a lender's money can flow: signed contracts, permits in hand, insurance bound, the independent engineer's report delivered. Financial close is the day the last one is ticked.

Measuring each cell's internal resistance or conductance as a fast proxy for its health, without discharging the string. It reliably finds the cell that has already failed; it does not prove how many minutes the string still holds.

What happens when the cheapest generation cannot reach the load because the wires between them are full. In most US markets it is priced rather than rationed, and it is the everyday form the transmission shortage takes.

A manufacturing contract in which the customer supplies some or all of the parts and pays only for the work. It keeps component pricing visible to the customer and keeps the inventory on the customer's books.

How a standby battery is really specified: the watts per cell it will hold for a stated time down to a stated end voltage at a stated temperature. Amp-hours describe a slow discharge and mislead badly at the rates a UPS actually uses.

A contract under which a project's former developer or a specialist manages construction for the new owner for a fee, without taking the EPC's fixed-price risk. It is how a seller keeps a role and a fee stream after selling the project.

A recurring commission review of a certified project while it is being built — schedule, spend against the certified cost, and whether the money so far was prudent — so cost overruns are examined as they happen rather than in one prudence review at the end. Georgia adopted it for Vogtle 3 and 4.

The exposure between financial close and the day the tenant starts paying: cost overruns, delays and the chance the tenant walks. In backstopped leases the guarantor's promise usually switches on only at rent commencement, so the build is the lender's risk.
Under the older two-step US licensing route, the authorisation to build a reactor. A separate operating licence is applied for later, once the plant is largely built.
Bank debt drawn during construction that converts into a long-term loan once the project is operating and its revenue can be measured. The conversion is where lenders re-test every assumption.

Money held inside a budget for the work that is certain to be needed and not yet identified. Whose contingency it is, and who keeps what is unspent, is a negotiated term rather than an accounting detail.

The generator rating for carrying a constant load at full output for unlimited hours a year, as a power station would. It is the most conservative of the standard ratings — the same engine carries a smaller number as continuous than as prime or standby — and the one a permanently islanded campus should be reading.

A firm that builds hardware to someone else's design and specification. The customer owns the design, the drawings and usually the tooling; the manufacturer sells labour, purchasing power and factory capacity.

Output power divided by input power for a converter — the rest leaves as heat. Efficiency is a curve, not a number: it collapses at light load and peaks somewhere below full load, so where a unit is parked on that curve matters as much as its headline figure.

One place in a power chain where electricity changes form or level — AC to DC, one DC voltage to another, one AC voltage to another. Each stage costs roughly one to three percent of the power as heat that must then be cooled, plus a box, floor space, and a way to fail; designing a power architecture is largely the art of deleting stages.

The plant at each end of an HVDC line that turns alternating current into direct current and back. It is the expensive, specialist part of the line — Siemens Energy's role on Grain Belt Express — and there is one per grid the line touches.

An open device that rejects heat by evaporating a small part of the water flowing through it into an air stream. It reaches a colder temperature than any air-cooled device can, and it consumes water to do so.

The engineering exercise that turns a one-line diagram into a set of protective-device settings: model every source and cable, compute the fault current available at each point, then choose relay curves and time delays so the nearest upstream device always clears first. Its outputs are relay settings, breaker trip units and the labels on the gear — and it is only true for the system it was drawn against.

The additive package in a coolant that coats metal surfaces so the fluid cannot attack them — typically tolyltriazole for copper and silicates for aluminium in a glycol blend. It depletes over time and has to be measured and re-dosed; a loop topped up with plain water quietly loses its protection.

The question of who pays for a shared upgrade — the customer whose request triggered it, everyone in the rate class, or every ratepayer. Cost-causation says whoever causes the cost pays it; socialization spreads it. Large-load tariffs, contribution-in-aid-of-construction rules and transmission cost allocation are all answers to the same question.

A ceiling on what a utility may recover from customers for a certified project. Costs above the cap fall on shareholders unless the commission later finds them prudent, which is why a certified cost figure matters as much to the utility as the approval itself.

The ratemaking method behind almost every US regulated utility: customers pay the utility's prudent costs of serving them — operations, fuel, depreciation, taxes — plus a return on the rate base. Rates are set by customer class, so the cost-of-service study is where the argument over who pays for a data center's substation is actually fought.

The sequence of parties between the owner of a building and the user of the computers inside it — landlord, tenant of record, operator, guarantor, chip lessor, end user. Each link carries a different risk and a different credit.

A large iron-cored inductor placed in series between the utility and a rotary UPS's synchronous machine, or between the units of an isolated-parallel bus. Because an inductor resists sudden changes in current, it lets the machine hold its output voltage clean while the supply behind it dips, distorts or fails, and it limits how much of a fault on one side is felt on the other.

Certificate of public convenience and necessity: the commission's permission to build a specific plant or line and put it into rate base. An IRP says what a utility expects to need; a CPCN is the docket in which it proves one project is needed, prudent and the right choice — and the order that turns a plan into a purchase.
aliases: certificate of public convenience and necessity

concepts.def: Computer room air conditioner: a self-contained refrigeration machine, compressor and all, sitting in the room it cools. Common on smaller sites where there is no central chilled-water plant to feed from.

Computer room air handler: a coil and fans fed with chilled water from a central plant, with no compressor of its own. Large facilities centralise the refrigeration in chillers and distribute cold water to many of these.

A promise by a strong third party to cover a weaker party's payments if that party fails — a guarantee in substance if not always in legal form. It lets a lease or loan be underwritten on the guarantor's credit rating rather than the borrower's.

The collateral a utility requires from a large new customer before it builds for it — a letter of credit, a cash deposit, a parent-company guaranty or a surety bond — sized to some months or years of the minimum bill, so that a customer that walks away leaves money behind rather than a stranded substation.

The electrical capacity reserved for the computers themselves — servers, storage, networking — excluding cooling, lighting and losses. Data-center leases are priced per megawatt of critical IT load; the building's gross capacity is larger.
The chain of activities whose durations add up to the project's finish date. Only work on this chain can make the project later, and only work on it can make it earlier.

When one customer class pays part of the cost of serving another. The live version: whether residential bills rise to pay for the generation and wires a data-center cluster requires — the finding regulators, legislatures and state auditors have been testing, and the political reason large-load tariffs exist.

Common Redundant Power Supply: the industry-standard shape, connector, and signaling for a server power-supply module, so any compliant vendor's unit fits any compliant server. Standardizing the slot is what turns server power into a contested commodity market rather than a per-vendor design.

Keeping fresh concrete moist and within a temperature range while it gains strength, which is a chemical reaction and not drying. Poorly cured concrete is permanently weaker and more prone to cracking.

How much current a converter or conductor delivers per unit of area, usually amps per square centimetre of board or package footprint. As chip currents climb past a thousand amps, the current density a regulator can achieve decides whether it fits beside — or beneath — the processor at all.

A converter that trades voltage for current at a fixed ratio — halve the voltage, double the current — much as a gear train trades speed for torque. In a factorized power chain it is the stage nearest the load, turning a modest current at a higher voltage into the very large current the chip needs at about one volt.

Making several converters or supplies that feed one bus each carry a fair fraction of the load instead of one hogging it. Without deliberate sharing, small differences in output voltage let one unit take everything and overheat while its neighbours idle.

A transformer whose job is measurement rather than power: it wraps a conductor and produces a small, proportional current a relay or meter can read safely. Its ratio is chosen so a relay sees a usable signal at both normal load and fault current, and a wrong ratio is one of the quiet ways a protection scheme fails to do what its settings say.

Being instructed to reduce output or consumption because the network cannot accommodate it at that moment. For a generator it is power that cannot be sold; for a very large load it is a contractual duty to back off — and a curtailment protocol is the document saying under what conditions, for how long, and who decides.

The share of a company's revenue coming from its largest customers. High concentration means the loss or slowdown of one relationship moves the whole company, which is why filings are required to disclose it.
Balancing the soil excavated from high areas against the soil needed in low ones, so that as little as possible is hauled on or off site. Haul is the expensive part, and the balance is designed.

Construction work in progress: plant that is being built but is not yet in service. Normally it earns no return until it is finished; a legislature or commission that lets CWIP into rate base lets the utility charge customers for a plant before it produces anything, which lowers financing cost and shifts construction risk toward customers.

How many full charge-discharge cycles a cell delivers before its capacity falls to a stated fraction of new — commonly 70 or 80 percent. It is the number a storage warranty is written around, and it is quoted against specific depth-of-discharge and temperature conditions, so two figures are only comparable when those conditions match.
How many times more concentrated the dissolved solids in a cooling tower's water are than in the make-up water. Running more cycles saves water and pushes the chemistry towards scaling and corrosion.

The laboratory crushing of test cylinders cast from a concrete pour, typically at seven and twenty-eight days, to prove the concrete reached its specified strength. A failed break stops everything that was going to sit on it.

The small fuel tank mounted at or near the gen-set, kept full by pumps from the bulk storage tank, that feeds the engine directly. Sizing it is a code and permit question as much as an engineering one, because the tank's capacity sets how long the set can run if the transfer pumps fail.

A breaker for direct current, which offers no zero crossing to help it. It has to force the current to zero itself — with a resonant circuit or with semiconductors — which is why DC breakers arrived decades after AC ones and still cost far more.

A converter that changes one DC voltage to another without passing through AC. It is the stage that does the work once power has arrived as direct current — inside a rack, inside a vehicle, or on a server board — and it is what lets a high-voltage DC bus feed low-voltage electronics.

The direct-current stage inside a static UPS between the rectifier and the inverter, where the battery connects. Every watt the load draws in double conversion passes through it as DC, which is why the batteries can take over without any switching event — they are already on the bus.

Data centre infrastructure management: software that inventories the physical plant — racks, circuits, cooling units, sensors — and monitors it as one live system. Its practical purpose is capacity planning: finding the power, cooling, space and redundancy that have been paid for and cannot currently be used.

Distribution cost recovery factor: a Texas rider that lets a wires utility recover new distribution investment between base rate cases, filed annually against a statutory formula. With interim transmission updates it is the reason a Texas TDU's earnings track its capital plan with only months of lag rather than years.

A deliberate pause in which both switches of a half-bridge are off, inserted so they can never be on together across the supply. Too little risks a destructive shoot-through; too much forces current through a body diode and wastes energy.

The heat a reactor keeps producing after the chain reaction stops, from the radioactive decay of fission products — roughly 6-7% of full power at shutdown, falling over hours and days. Removing it is the central safety problem of every reactor.
The short length of pipe joining the primary and secondary loops of a chilled-water plant. Which way water flows through it, and how much, is the plant's most useful single diagnostic.

A rate mechanism that separates a utility's revenue from the volume of energy it sells, so that selling less does not cut its earnings and selling more does not raise them — with a true-up each year. It removes the utility's incentive to oppose efficiency, and it changes what data-center load growth is worth to it: under full decoupling the growth pays for wires, not profit.
Piles or drilled shafts that carry load past unsuitable near-surface soil to competent material below. They are chosen when the ground near the surface cannot be made good enough.
The gradual loss of a battery's usable capacity with cycling and age. Storage contracts manage it with capacity guarantees and planned augmentation.

A loan that is committed up front but drawn in tranches as the borrower needs cash — typically as equipment is ordered or construction milestones are hit. Common for GPU fleets and data-center builds, where spending is staged.

The small fraction of fission neutrons (under one percent) emitted seconds to minutes after the split rather than instantly. They are the reason a reactor responds on a human timescale and can be controlled at all.

The chance that contracted capacity arrives later than the date the buyer planned around. For a compute buyer whose demand is growing, a late site means rationing customers; for the lender, a delayed backstop.

A dated point at which contracted capacity must be energized and handed over. Rent, guarantees and investor money are often tied to milestones — a missed one can delay a backstop, trigger a termination right or hold back funding.

The temperature difference between the water returning to a chiller and the water leaving it. A plant is designed around a delta-T, and the flow it must pump for a given duty is inversely proportional to it.

The part of a large customer's bill priced per kilowatt of peak demand rather than per kilowatt-hour of energy used. It pays for the wires and plant that have to exist to serve the customer's maximum draw, whether or not that draw occurs often — which is why a data center's bill is mostly demand, not energy.

A program that pays a customer to cut its grid draw when the system is stressed — by shedding load or by switching to on-site generation. Running backup engines for it moves them out of the emergency-only class, which is why the permit, not the machine, decides whether a data center can join.

Operating equipment below its nameplate rating because real conditions — ambient temperature, altitude, state of charge, or age — do not match the conditions the rating assumed. A specification read as a guaranteed operating number rather than a rated one is one of the most common sources of a capacity shortfall that presents as an equipment fault.

The party contractually entitled to approve a change to the product — a component substitution, a layout revision, a supplier swap. Confusion about who holds it is the most common cause of a manufacturing dispute.
A delivery method in which one entity holds both the design and the construction contracts, so the owner has a single point of responsibility and the two disciplines cannot blame each other.

Regulatory approval of a standardised reactor design, once, independent of any site — so that later applicants reference the approved design instead of re-litigating it. Approving the design and licensing the site are two different clocks.

The years between a component being chosen for a product and that product shipping in volume. In power semiconductors it means today's revenue was decided by decisions taken two or three years ago, and today's decisions will not show up in revenue for as long again.

The life a battery is designed to reach under ideal float conditions, quoted in years. It is not the life it will get: temperature, cycling and ripple decide the service life, which is routinely a fraction of the design figure.

Being selected as the supplier for a component in a product that is about to be built — decided during the customer's design phase, often years before volume revenue. Once designed in, a part is expensive to replace, so the win locks in the socket for that product's life.

A developer that keeps the projects it builds and earns the operating cash flow for decades. Needs long-term capital and an operations team; the reward is the whole life of the asset rather than one sale.

A developer that carries a project through permits, interconnection and contracts, then sells it to an owner before or at construction. Capital-light and quick; the price depends on which development stage the project has reached.

The difference between what a developer spent to bring a project to a saleable stage and the price a buyer pays for it — the profit on origination. It is earned on sale, not on operation, and is rarely disclosed.

Every project a developer is working on that is not yet built, from a land option to a permitted, contracted site awaiting financing. Rankings by pipeline megawatts measure ambition and options, not operating capacity.

The sequence a project climbs from idea to operation: site control, interconnection request, permits, offtake, notice to proceed, financial close, construction, commercial operation. Each rung retires a risk, so each rung raises what a buyer will pay.

The temperature at which the room's air begins to condense water on a surface. Coolant supplied below it sweats every hose and cold plate onto the boards beneath, so a CDU holds its supply temperature above the data hall's dew point — one reason warm-water cooling is safer than cold.

Diesel exhaust fluid: the urea-and-water solution injected into the exhaust ahead of an SCR catalyst, where it converts nitrogen oxides into nitrogen and water. A Tier 4 engine cannot meet its emissions limit without it, so DEF supply and freeze protection become part of the site's operating plan.

A filter in the exhaust that traps soot and is periodically burned clean. Together with SCR it is the after-treatment that separates a Tier 4 engine from a Tier 2 one, and it adds backpressure, heat and maintenance the standby duty cycle does not otherwise need.

A simulated copy of a real asset, fed by its live data, used to rehearse changes before they touch the hardware — testing a control strategy, forecasting degradation, or learning what normal looks like so anomalies stand out. It is how an operator tries something on a plant without trying it on the plant.

A data-center lease signed by the end user itself, in its own name, rather than by a cloud provider or intermediary on its behalf. It gives the user control of the site and puts the user's own credit behind the rent.

Cooling servers by circulating liquid through cold plates bolted onto the processors, memory and other hot parts, instead of blowing air over them. Single-phase DLC keeps the fluid liquid throughout; the heat leaves the rack in a coolant loop and is handed to the building at a coolant distribution unit.
The final treatment step that inactivates pathogens — chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light. Which method is used changes what residual protection the water carries downstream.

Who decides when a battery charges and discharges. Under a toll or service agreement the buyer holds them; under a merchant model the owner does — and the holder of dispatch rights holds most of the revenue risk.

Generation that can be turned on, up, down or off when the grid operator asks — gas, nuclear, hydro, and storage for as long as its energy lasts — as opposed to output that follows the weather. A plan that must serve a data center's flat load at night still buys dispatchable capacity, which is why gas keeps appearing in resource plans written under clean-energy mandates.

ERCOT's registration class for a generator or battery connected to a distribution system rather than the transmission grid — typically under 10 MW. It follows a lighter interconnection path than a transmission-connected resource, which is why developers size projects at 9.9 MW.

UPS topologies that reach N+1 or better without doubling everything. In a block-redundant or catcher design a spare UPS system stands ready to take any block's load through static transfer switches; in a distributed-redundant design each load is fed from two of several systems so any one can fail. Both cost less than 2N, and both place the redundancy in a switching event that has to work.

In ERCOT, the company that owns the local distribution network a small generator connects to — Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP. A distribution-connected battery's interconnection is negotiated with the DSP, not with ERCOT's transmission planners.

The ratio between the sum of a facility's individual maximum demands and the maximum demand of the whole facility, which is always lower because loads do not all peak together. It is the number that lets a designer buy less generation than the nameplate sum of everything connected — and the number an AI training hall attacks, because thousands of accelerators can peak in step.

Dry low-NOx combustion: premixing fuel and air before the flame so the mixture burns lean and cool enough to form little nitrogen oxide, without injecting water or steam to do it. Lean premixed flames sit close to blowing out and close to travelling back up the burner, so the combustor is the part of a gas turbine most constrained by the fuel it is asked to burn.

A commission's case file: a numbered proceeding holding the application, testimony, discovery, intervenor filings, hearing transcripts and the final order. For a seller the docket is the only place a utility's plans are stated under oath with dates attached — read the docket, not the press release.

The UPS mode in which all power is rectified to DC and re-made as AC by the inverter, continuously, so the load always sees a synthesized waveform and never the raw supply. It is the highest grade of protection — VFI in the IEC classification — and costs a few percent of every megawatt-hour as conversion heat; eco-mode is the alternative that idles the conversion and accepts a transfer.

A circuit breaker that racks in and out of its cell on rails, with three defined positions: connected, test (control power live, main contacts isolated) and disconnected. It lets a breaker be tested or replaced without de-energizing the bus behind it, which is why medium-voltage switchgear is built this way and why racking is one of the highest-exposure tasks in an electrical room.

A single release of loan money to a project during construction, made against a certificate that the work it pays for has been done. The independent engineer's monthly construction-monitoring report is what the lender relies on before signing each one.
Liquid water carried out of a cooling tower as droplets in the exhaust air, as distinct from water that has evaporated. It is small, it is regulated, and it carries whatever is in the basin with it.

The lightly doped layer inside a power transistor that absorbs the voltage when the device is off. It has to be thicker for a higher voltage rating, and every micron of thickness adds resistance when the device is on — the trade at the heart of power-device design.

A governor setting that lets an engine's speed fall slightly as its load rises, so several engines sharing a bus each take a predictable share of the load instead of fighting over it. Its partner is isochronous control, which holds speed exactly constant and is given to one machine or to the paralleling controller so the bus frequency stays put.

Diesel rotary uninterruptible power supply: a rotary UPS whose flywheel and synchronous machine share a shaft line with a diesel engine through a clutch. When the supply fails the flywheel carries the load for the seconds the engine needs to start and clutch in, so one machine does the work of UPS, transfer switch and generator — with no battery and no separate transfer.
Air temperature as an ordinary thermometer reads it. An air-cooled machine rejects heat against this, which is why it is less efficient than a tower on the same day.
A closed-loop finned coil that rejects heat from a fluid straight to ambient air, with no evaporation and no water. It trades efficiency and hot-day capacity for using no water at all.

A transformer insulated and cooled by air or solid resin instead of oil. It carries no fire load and no oil-containment requirement, so it can sit inside a building, but it is larger, noisier and less efficient than an equivalent oil-filled unit and does not scale as far up in rating.

Debt service coverage ratio: the cash a project earns in a period divided by the debt payments due in it. Lenders size a loan so that the ratio stays above a floor in their downside case, which is why a merchant battery borrows less per megawatt than a tolled one.
Equipment with two power supplies fed from two independent paths, so either path can be lost or worked on without the load noticing. It is what makes a whole side of a data hall maintainable at once.

Qualifying two suppliers for the same item so neither can hold the buyer hostage on price or availability. It costs money — two qualifications, two tool sets, split volume that raises unit cost — which is why it is an argued decision rather than a default.
How long a storage plant can discharge at full power (energy divided by power, MWh ÷ MW). Duration decides which grid jobs a battery can do — most US grid-scale projects run a few hours.

A power room built and wired in a factory, tested as a unit, then shipped to site as a walk-in enclosure — switchgear, transformers, controls, lighting, HVAC and cable already in place. It converts skilled field electrical labour into factory labour and moves the schedule risk from the site to the shop, at the price of shipping weight, crane access and a design frozen much earlier.

A landowner's grant of a right to use a strip of land — for a transmission line, the right to build and maintain towers and conductors across a farm. A long line needs thousands; the ones a developer cannot buy voluntarily are the ones it seeks by eminent domain.

The Experimental Breeder Reactor II, a sodium-cooled fast reactor that ran at Idaho from 1964 to 1994 and in 1986 survived deliberate loss-of-flow and loss-of-heat-sink tests at full power with no operator action. Most US fast-reactor design heritage traces to it.

Running a static UPS with the load on the raw supply through the bypass and the conversion stage idling in reserve, lifting efficiency toward 98–99 percent. The bet is that the unit can detect a supply failure and transfer back to the inverter inside the servers' hold-up time, for every kind of fault — which is exactly what the mode's critics doubt.

The share of a company's profits and value an investor is entitled to, as distinct from control. CDPQ holds 52.4 per cent economic ownership of Invenergy Renewables while management remains the managing member that runs the business.

Effective load carrying capability: how much of a resource's nameplate a grid operator counts toward meeting peak — its accredited capacity. A four-hour battery or a solar farm is credited well below nameplate and a gas plant close to it, so accreditation decides how many megawatts of storage a utility must build to satisfy a reserve requirement and how much a battery earns in a capacity market.

A public utility commission whose members are chosen by voters rather than appointed by a governor. Its decisions on rates and plants carry directly into election campaigns, so affordability politics reach the docket faster than in an appointed state — and a single election can change who decides the next case.

Colorado's name for the integrated resource plan: a two-phase docket in which the commission first approves the need and the resource envelope, then a competitive solicitation is run and the commission selects the winning bids from the utility's shortlist in a second decision. Phase two is where the developers, and therefore the equipment, are actually chosen.

Electric service agreement: the contract between a utility and one large customer that fixes the megawatts to be served, the term, the minimum bill, collateral and exit terms — the document that turns a request for load into an obligation the utility can finance a plant against.

How thickly the active material is coated onto a cell's current collectors. Thick electrodes hold more energy per litre and make the ions travel further; thin ones deliver current hard and store less. It is the single design choice that separates a power cell from an energy cell.

The industry of building electronics for other companies, spanning bare circuit-board assembly through full product assembly, test, distribution and repair. Its economics are volume and purchasing scale, so margins are thin and the winners are large.

A steel plate, anchor bolt, rail or bracket cast into concrete while it is wet, so something can later be bolted to it. Once the pour has cured, a missing embed becomes a drilled, tested and disputed repair.

The regulatory class for a stationary engine that runs only when the normal supply fails, plus a small annual allowance of hours for testing and maintenance. The class is what lets a backup fleet be permitted quickly and without the strictest emission controls — and it is lost the moment the same engines are run for prime power, peak shaving or a demand-response payment.

The area around a reactor within which off-site emergency plans must exist. Shrinking it is one of the concrete practical claims small designs make, and it is decided by the regulator against the source term, not by the vendor.

The legal power to take private land for a public use in exchange for compensation. A transmission line with a state certificate can use it against holdout landowners, which is why certificates are fought so hard in court.

Energy management system: the supervisory software that decides when a storage plant charges and discharges — following price signals, grid instructions, or a contract — and coordinates the PCS and BMS to do it.

The voltage at which a discharge is declared over — chosen by the system rather than by the chemistry, because below it the inverter can no longer work with what the string is delivering. Set it lower and you buy minutes at the cost of life.

The moment new electrical infrastructure is first put under live voltage and proven, with the utility present. It is the line between contracted megawatts and connected ones: before it, a connection agreement is a promise; after it, power can actually flow, and every schedule upstream of it is measured against this date.

Buying electricity when it is cheap (midday solar, overnight) to sell it when it is dear (evening peak). For a battery the profit is the price spread minus round-trip losses, and it is the revenue left once ancillary-service prices fall.

A battery optimized for how much it holds and how many times it can be emptied and refilled — sized by hours of duration and judged on cycle life and cost per stored unit. A grid storage container is the archetype, and it is the near-inverse of a power battery in almost every design choice.

The part of a bill priced per kilowatt-hour consumed — fuel and the variable cost of running plants. For a flat, always-on load it is large in total but it is the demand charge, not the energy charge, that decides whether the customer has paid for the capacity built to serve it.
An extra federal tax credit for projects sited in places with closed coal plants or mines or high fossil-fuel employment. Building a battery on a retired coal station earns it.

How much energy a cell stores per litre — or per kilogram — of itself. It is the figure of merit for a grid or vehicle cell, and it trades directly against the electrode design that lets a cell deliver current hard.

A wholesale market design with no capacity market: generators are paid only for the energy they actually sell, and the incentive to build new plant comes from prices that spike when supply is scarce. ERCOT is the US example — no auction pays a plant to exist, so no commission certifies one, and whether a plant gets built is a private investment decision made against expected scarcity prices.

A site where large generation, storage and a large customer — a data centre, a hydrogen plant — are built together behind one grid connection, so most of the power never crosses the public grid. The developer sells the whole package rather than power alone.

A contract in which a utility or public power agency pays a fixed fee for the right to use a battery's capacity for a term of years, leaving dispatch to the buyer. It is the public-power form of a tolling agreement.

The licensed engineer who signs and seals a project's design and carries legal responsibility for it. On a turnkey EPC job it works for the contractor; on a multi-contract job the owner's engineer may hold the seal — which decides who answers when the design is wrong.

Raising the share of the fissile isotope uranium-235 above the 0.7% found in nature. The higher the enrichment, the more compact a core can be — and the tighter the security and transport rules become.

What a whole business is worth including its debt. Equity value is what the owners receive after the debt is counted, so a USD 7 billion enterprise value with USD 3 billion of equity value implies about USD 4 billion of debt.

A contract in which a buyer purchases the renewable-energy certificates from a project without taking the electricity, which is sold into the grid. Meta's 2024 Invenergy deals were structured this way; the buyer gets the clean-energy claim, the project gets a fixed revenue stream.

The US emission stage most large standby data-center engines are certified to, available because an engine that only runs in emergencies is regulated far more loosely than one that runs for a living. It is why the same engine block is sold as a cheap Tier 2 standby set and an expensive Tier 4 prime set.
Engineering, procurement, and construction: the contractor model that delivers a plant turnkey under one contract — and the label for the firms that do it.

A thin crystal layer grown on top of a wafer to a precisely controlled thickness and doping. In a power device it is the drift region, so its quality sets both the voltage the part can hold off and how many good parts a wafer yields.

The engineered concrete base under a transformer, generator, chiller or tower, sized for its weight, its dynamic loads and its maintenance access. It has to exist before the equipment can be set, which puts it on the critical path.

An order to buy machinery — here generators — outright, with delivery on a schedule, as opposed to a power-purchase agreement in which someone else owns the plant and sells the output. The buyer owns the risk and the asset.

The share of a utility's regulatory capital structure funded by equity rather than debt. Regulators set it for ratemaking regardless of how the company actually finances itself. A higher equity ratio raises the allowed return in dollars, because equity earns the authorized return on equity while debt earns only its interest cost.

The Texas grid operator. An energy-only market with its own interconnection process — faster to connect, more volatile to operate in — which is why so much US storage and data-center buildout lands in Texas.

An employee stock ownership plan: a trust that holds company shares on behalf of employees, who receive an ownership account rather than buying in. It is a retirement plan and an ownership structure at once.

The European Union's emission stage for non-road and stationary engines — the counterpart to the US EPA tiers, and stricter than Tier 4 on particle number. A gen-set sold into both markets is certified twice, which is one reason European and American versions of the same product carry different after-treatment.
The heat exchanger where the refrigerant boils and takes heat out of the water being chilled. In a chiller it is where the useful cooling actually happens.

The DC current fed to a synchronous machine's rotor winding to create its magnetic field. Raising it lifts the output voltage and the reactive power the machine supplies; the automatic voltage regulator adjusts it continuously, and it is how a rotary UPS or a synchronous condenser holds voltage through a disturbance.

What a large customer owes if it leaves a utility contract before the term ends — typically the remaining minimum bills, or the unrecovered cost of the plant and wires built for it. With the term, the ramp and the credit support it is one of the four terms that make a data-center tariff financeable.
The valve or orifice that drops the high-pressure liquid refrigerant back to evaporator pressure, cooling it as it goes. The cheapest component in the loop and the one that meters the whole machine.
A contractual right, not an obligation, for a customer to take more capacity later at pre-agreed terms. Headlines count options as if exercised; balance sheets do not.
Clay that swells when it takes on water and shrinks when it dries, moving whatever sits on it. It is treated by removing it, stabilising it, or spanning over it — never by ignoring it.
The European rules capping and reducing fluorinated-gas supply and banning specific uses on a schedule. It runs ahead of the US phasedown and is why some product lines change in Europe first.

The building's own cooling-water loop — the plant side of a coolant distribution unit — connected to chillers, cooling towers or dry coolers where the heat finally leaves the site. Larger, at whatever temperature the plant can make, and treated to plant rather than electronics standards, it never touches the servers.

A power-chain design that splits the two jobs a converter normally does — holding the voltage steady (regulation) and changing its level (transformation) — into separate stages, so each can be built where it works best. The regulator lives upstream where the current is small, and a fixed-ratio current multiplier lives next to the load where the current is enormous.

Testing assembled equipment at the manufacturer's works, with the customer present, before it ships. It catches wiring and logic errors while the fix is cheap and the gear is still accessible — but it can only prove what can be simulated in a shop, so an integrated test on site under real load is still the thing that proves the system.

Flexible AC transmission systems: the family of power-electronic devices — shunt and series compensation, STATCOMs, phase shifters — that make power flow in an AC network controllable instead of merely the arithmetic consequence of impedance.

The investment vehicle of a wealthy family, which can own operating businesses outright and hold them without a fund's fixed life. A family-owned developer answers to no limited partners and need not sell on a schedule.

Selling part of a project or portfolio — often a majority — to a long-term owner while keeping a stake and the operating role. It recycles a developer's capital into the next project; WEC Energy Group's majority ownership of Invenergy-built solar plants is the pattern.

An ERCOT ancillary service that pays a battery to inject power within a fraction of a second when grid frequency drops. Batteries are almost the only resource fast enough, which made it an early revenue source for Texas batteries.

A reactor that fissions with unmoderated, high-energy neutrons. Fission is less likely per neutron, so the fuel must be more enriched and the core more compact — but the neutrons that are left can do things thermal neutrons cannot.

The current that flows into a short circuit before a breaker clears it — many times the normal load current. A protection scheme needs enough of it to be sure the right breaker trips fast: a rotating machine delivers a large surge from its stored magnetic energy, while an inverter can supply only a little more than its rating, which changes how the downstream protection must be designed.

Foreign entity of concern: a US legal designation (tied to China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea) that disqualifies projects and products with too much such involvement from federal tax credits — a central bankability question for China-linked battery supply.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission: the US regulator of interstate transmission, wholesale power markets and the regional grid operators. State commissions set retail rates and certify plants; FERC sets the transmission tariff and approves the market rules and interconnection procedures the state-level story sits on top of.

How most interstate transmission is priced: a formula, approved by FERC, that turns the transmission owner's booked costs and rate base into an annual revenue requirement, updated every year without a contested case. It is the reason transmission is a utility's most predictable earnings line and why a regional plan award converts into earnings so smoothly.

Funds from operations: the cash a company generates from running its business before working-capital swings. Rating agencies judge a utility mainly on FFO as a percentage of its debt, so a large capital plan financed with borrowing pushes that ratio down — and a utility whose ratio approaches the agency's stated downgrade threshold has to raise equity, sell an asset or slow the plan.

A single number that multiplies a device's on-resistance by a switching-related charge, so two switches can be compared on conduction and switching cost together. Lower is better, and it is how a datasheet argument about one material beating another is usually settled.

The date on which a project's loan agreements become effective and money can be drawn: every condition precedent satisfied, every adviser's report delivered. Construction schedules, equipment slots and tax-credit deadlines all hang on hitting it.
The fund or firm that owns a company's equity and can write the next cheque. Lenders price a project partly on who the sponsor is, and a change of sponsor can change the terms of every loan.

Dividing a building with rated walls and floors so that a fire and its smoke stay in one part of it for a stated number of hours. Every penetration through such a wall has to be sealed to the same rating.

How hot the gas is where it first meets the turbine blades — the single number a gas turbine's efficiency and output track most closely. Every extra hundred degrees buys efficiency and costs materials science: single-crystal blades, ceramic coatings and cooling air bled from the compressor, which is itself a loss. Modern heavy-duty machines are described by class as 1,600°C or 1,650°C.

The grid operator's last resort: ordering utilities to cut power to ordinary customers because supply cannot meet demand. Texas's 2025 large-load law ties the biggest customers to it — during an emergency the operator may direct a large load to run its backup generation or curtail before, or instead of, cutting homes.

Adding a controllable resource — gas engines, turbines or a long-duration battery — to a renewable site so the customer's load is met in the hours the sun and wind cannot cover. It is what turns a solar-and-wind campus into round-the-clock supply.

A formal check of the first units off a production tool against every dimension and requirement on the drawing. Passing it is what turns a prototype process into an approved one, and it is a contractual milestone, not a courtesy.

The first unit of a new design, which pays for every lesson the design has not yet learned. Its cost is not evidence about the tenth unit, and treating it as such is the commonest error in reading a new-technology cost claim.

Splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter fragments, releasing energy and two or three free neutrons. Those neutrons are what make a chain reaction possible: the energy is a by-product of a neutron economy.

How fast a flame front travels through a fuel-air mixture. Hydrogen's is several times methane's, which is the root of most of the engineering in hydrogen-capable combustors: a flame that outruns the incoming mixture stops sitting where it was designed to sit.

A premixed flame travelling upstream into the burner it should be sitting in front of, because the mixture's flame speed has overtaken the flow feeding it. Hardware not designed for it melts. It is the specific failure mode that limits how much hydrogen a dry low-NOx combustor can take.

Measurable — sometimes visible — fluctuation of voltage caused by a load that changes fast and repeatedly. It is the classic symptom of a large swinging load connected at a point that is not strong enough for it.

The small continuous voltage held across a standby battery to keep it full without overcharging it. Nearly all of a UPS battery's life is spent floating, and the float voltage together with the room temperature decides how long that life is.

How level and how wavy a finished concrete floor is, expressed as F-numbers measured within days of the pour. A floor flat enough for an office is not necessarily flat enough for a row of racks on castors.

The weight per unit area a floor is allowed to carry. It decides where battery strings, large UPS frames and transformers may stand, and in retrofits it settles more equipment arguments than price does.

Making every rack on a shared coolant header receive its share of flow, since coolant takes the easiest path and the nearest or least-restricted racks would otherwise starve the far ones. Done with balancing valves or orifices at each manifold, reverse-return piping and a pump held to a pressure setpoint.
